title: runtime-failure-telemetry-convergence-and-signal-fabric
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a unified failure-signal fabric that converges tracing hooks, metric derivation, and log enrichment so dashboards and SLOs reflect a single, debuggable failure taxonomy. Scope: 1) Define canonical failure class schema (timeout, overload, model_error, rpc_client_error, rpc_server_error, resource_exhaustion, data_error, retry_violation). 2) Implement tracehook adapters in runtime exec paths to attach normalized failure tags and correlation ids (request_id, route_id, model_variant, host_region). 3) Expand metrics/log pipeline to derive low-cardinality error signals (failure_bucket, % of requests by failure class) and high-cardinality debug indices (span_id->trace_id mappings) persisted to ClickHouse for drilldowns. 4) New Grafana dashboards: failure-fabric-overview, per-route timeout heatmap, overload-pressure vs queue-depth, model-error waterfall (kernel fallback -> OOM -> logits-NaN), and SLA breach explorer. Success metrics: 90% of production errors tagged with canonical class within 2 hours of rollout; dashboards show 99th percentile of affected routes; alerts reduce oncall mean-time-to-diagnose by 30%. Acceptance criteria: - Tracehooks exist for frontend router, scheduler, and model worker paths and attach canonical tags. - Ingestion pipeline emits derived metrics with documented cardinality limits. - Dashboards deployed to console-2025.03 and validated in staging. Design notes/trade-offs: - We'll use a two-tier signal approach: compact aggregated metrics (Prometheus) for alerting, detailed indices (ClickHouse) for post-mortem. This balances cost vs debugability. - Sampling: 1% tail-sampling for traces generally, with deterministic promotion for failure-class samples; synthetic slow-path sampling enabled for routes with >1% timeout rate. - Enrichment will be performed at the tracehook layer where possible to minimize downstream join costs; however, some tags (kernel_selection, quantized_model_variant) will be added in post-ingest processors because model workers can't write to tracing API synchronously without perf impact. - Cardinality controls: limit route/model tags to top N per org and map the rest to "other" to protect Prometheus series. Implementation plan (phased): Phase 1 (2 sprints): canonical schema, tracehook adapter prototype in runtime, demo dashboard. Phase 2 (2 sprints): pipeline processors to derive metrics and ClickHouse schema, dashboard expansion, alert rules. Phase 3 (1 sprint): rollout to production, runbook, docs, retro. Risks: high-cardinality explosion, tracing latency if enrichment is synchronous, incomplete model-worker metadata. Mitigations: asynchronous enrichment path, bounded tag whitelist, preflight tests on staging. Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Signal+Fabric+Spec; Design board: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SignalFabricDesign; Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4221; Dashboard proto: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/failure-fabric-overview (staging).
